concerns.text: T025b instructs to 'commit this artifact to git' (raw_translations_log.csv). This violates Constitution Principle III (Data Hygiene) and Principle I (Reproducibility) which mandate that raw data (LLM outputs) must NOT be committed to git to avoid PII exposure and repository bloat. The task weakens the constitutional constraint by treating raw experimental data as version-controlled source code.

T027a mandates selecting a specific deterministic transpiler (transcrypt/pyjs) to convert Python tests to JavaScript. This contradicts spec.md (Assumption about test translation) and plan.md (Constitution Check VII) which rely on the LLM or an unverified 'dedicated transpiler' mechanism. By forcing a specific tool that may not exist or be deterministic for the specific test patterns, the task introduces a high risk of blocking the entire US3 workflow, effectively weakening the feasibility of FR-003.

T010 instructs creating 'placeholder files' for prompt conditions without defining the actual prompt text. This violates Constitution Principle VI (Prompt Specification Integrity) which requires prompt templates to be stored as version-controlled text with exact content. Creating empty placeholders fails to satisfy the requirement to 'store prompt templates' and leaves the core experimental variable undefined, weakening the reproducibility constraint.

Tasks T033-T035 introduce 'failure topology' analysis (categorizing rigidity, confabulation, etc.) which is not present in spec.md Functional Requirements (FR-001 through FR-006) or Success Criteria. This constitutes scope creep in the task list, as no requirement exists to classify failure modes or generate a topology report, potentially consuming budget/time not allocated in the spec and violating the constraint of strict requirement adherence.
